facts.label: NASA Moon Base planned investment, Phases 1 and 2, as spoken

sources.name: Spaceflight Now, NASA outlines ambitious $20 billion plan for moon base, William Harwood, March 25, 2026
The Planetary Society, Ignition: A new series of NASA initiatives, March 24, 2026
sources.tier_note: Tier-2 outlet, tier-4 claim. On this figure it did no institutional analysis: it repeated a podium remark and attributed it to documents on NASA's website that nobody has produced. The reputation was earned on work it did not do here.

facts.notes: Spoken, not published, and the record has ONE independent source: both entries trace to the same sentence, Isaacman at the March 24, 2026 Ignition event, quoted by Spaceflight Now as 'we will invest approximately $20 billion over the next seven years.' Two printings of one utterance are one source. No NASA document is verified to print any dollar figure for the Moon Base, not $20B and not $10B per phase: the Building the Moon Base fact sheet (nasa.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/building-the-moon-base-1.pdf, tier 1, opened by Enzo 2026-07-17) gives phase structure and dates only, Phase 1 (Now-2029) Experiment, Learn; Phase 2 (2029-2032) Early Habitation; Phase 3 (2032 and beyond) Sustained Human Presence. The Ignition presentation (2-building-the-moon-base.pdf) corroborates that the program is phased, which is what it actually supports; an earlier agent read claiming per-phase dollar figures and different dates is withdrawn and must not be used. OPEN ITEM, BLOCKING PROMOTION: that 31MB presentation is the only NASA artifact that may print per-phase dollars and has not been opened by Enzo. Until it is, no dollar figure on this site claims a NASA document as its source. The tier-1 record of the utterance is NASA's webcast video (youtube.com/live/yIlTwwJv1Ac), not verifiable as text. Planned investment, not an appropriation; the FY2027 request has no $20B line item. Do not conflate with the $6B CLPS 2.0 cap. The 'seven years' from the same sentence has its own record, moonbase.program.duration_years.

facts.label: NASA Moon Base planned investment window, as spoken

sources.name: Spaceflight Now, NASA outlines ambitious $20 billion plan for moon base, William Harwood, March 25, 2026
The Planetary Society, Ignition: A new series of NASA initiatives, March 24, 2026
sources.tier_note: Tier-2 outlet, tier-4 claim. Same departure as on moonbase.program.total: a repeated podium remark with an invented paper provenance, not institutional analysis.

facts.notes: Spoken, not published, from the same sentence as the $20B: 'we will invest approximately $20 billion over the next seven years,' Isaacman, Ignition, March 24, 2026. ONE independent source: both entries trace to that utterance and count as one. The seven is quoted speech in print, not a count of phase dates, so it is reported. What NASA's written record says (Building the Moon Base fact sheet, opened by Enzo 2026-07-17): Phase 1 (Now-2029), Phase 2 (2029-2032), Phase 3 (2032 and beyond); phase dates, no duration, no dollars. The tension, recorded and not resolved: Phases 1 and 2 span roughly 2026 to 2032, which is six elapsed years or seven counted inclusively, and the fiscal-versus-calendar question is unresolved because NASA does not say. Some trade coverage frames the window as FY2027-2033. Record the disagreement; do not pick a winner. An earlier agent read of the Ignition presentation (Phase 1 2026-2028, Phase 3 2033-2036) matches neither fact sheet and is withdrawn. OPEN ITEM, BLOCKING PROMOTION: the 31MB Ignition presentation is unopened. If NASA restates the window, this record changes and every figure derived from it moves with it.

facts.label: US resident population, July 1, 2025

sources.name: US Census Bureau press release, U.S. Population Growth Slows Due to Historic Decline in Net International Migration, January 27, 2026

facts.notes: Vintage 2025 estimate, stated in the release as 341.8 million as of July 1, 2025. The detailed table (NST-EST2025-POP) carries full precision; the printed figure is used here. Rev 01 of the data model used 342e6 as a literal; this record replaces it, and the difference moves the per-person figure by about 4 cents. The denominator choice itself (resident population vs tax returns vs net positive payers) is contested and is named on every fact derived from this one.

derived.label: Global space spending per second, at 2024's rate
derived.notes: Rate visualization, not a measurement. 2024's annual estimate divided into 31,536,000 seconds (a 365-day year). The vintage is the choice: 2024 is the latest full year published.

derived.label: Moon Base dollars committed to date, including options
derived.notes: Warning, and it travels with this number everywhere it renders: the total includes Blue Origin's $280.4M option period, which has not been exercised. The base total, options excluded, is $1.292B. Publishing the headline $1.6B without this note is the exact species of imprecision this publication exists to correct.

derived.label: Moon Base dollars committed to date, options excluded
derived.notes: Base awards only. Excludes Blue Origin's unexercised $280.4M option period. The with-options figure is moonbase.committed.total.

derived.label: Share of the planned Moon Base investment that is signed
derived.notes: Numerator includes Blue Origin's unexercised $280.4M option. Denominator is the approximately $20B planned Phase 1 and 2 investment, a spoken figure, not an appropriation. Both choices are named because both move the percentage. Stored as a fraction; the percent unit converts at render.

derived.label: Committed to pressurized habitats
derived.notes: Evaluates to zero because no habitat award exists in the ledger as of the ledger's own as_of date. This is Burn Rate's count of the award record, not a figure NASA published. NASA does not publish absences. Arithmetic over an empty set is a derived fact by construction, and this is the only number on the site for which Burn Rate is the primary source. The day a habitat award lands in the ledger, this figure stops being zero everywhere it renders, in the same commit.

derived.label: Committed to lunar surface power
derived.notes: Evaluates to zero because no surface-power award exists in the ledger as of the ledger's own as_of date. This is Burn Rate's count of the award record, not a figure NASA published. NASA does not publish absences. The open NextSTEP-3 Appendix B directed call is a separate, reported record; the day its award lands, this figure stops being zero everywhere it renders, in the same commit.

derived.label: Days since the last Moon Base award
derived.notes: Computed at render time from the latest award date in the ledger. Live by definition.

derived.label: Moon Base cost per American per year
derived.notes: The denominator is a choice and it is contested: population.us is the total US resident population, Census Vintage 2025 estimate, 341.8 million as of July 1, 2025. Tax returns or net positive taxpayers each give a different answer. The window is the spoken seven years, moonbase.program.duration_years, which carries its own phase-date tension. Roughly $8.36 per American per year.
